title: The word with 645 meanings
hook: The small verb run has more meanings in the Oxford dictionary than any other word.
peek: When the Oxford English Dictionary revised the verb run, its entry grew to about 645 distinct senses. That pushed past put and set, earlier record holders, and made run the English word with the most meanings.
lede: The Oxford English Dictionary records about 645 senses for the verb run, from running a race to running a business, a tap or a fever. That count came from the dictionary's revision of the entry, published in 2011, and it overtook put, the record holder since 2007, and set, which had led with around 430 senses in the second edition of 1989.

bullets.text: The lexicographer Peter Gilliver reportedly spent about nine months working through the evidence for run. Each sense needs its own definition and dated quotations showing how it has been used.

Set had been the dictionary's biggest entry for decades, until revised entries for make and then put passed it. Run beat them all partly because the language changed: machines, computers and programs all run, and each new use added senses.
The longest entries tend to belong to short, old verbs like run, set, put and take. They get used so often, in so many phrases, that their meanings keep branching.
